name: Knochenhaueramtshaus

dates.altered: Restored 1853-1854 under the city architect Carl Schuette; destroyed in 1945; rebuilt 1986-1989 together with the Baeckeramtshaus at Markt 8. Both reconstructions were entered in the monument register in 2017.
dates.note: The 1529 date was documented by an inscription over the ground-floor entrance in Gothic minuscules, which the German Wikipedia article prints: 'Anno ∙ Dnj ∙ Dusent ∙ vyffhundert ∙ twitich ∙ vde ∙ neghen.' The node's exemplar year agrees.

refs.title: Niedersaechsisches Denkmalverzeichnis, as reported by the German Wikipedia article
refs.note: NO NUMBER IS CARRIED because none was read. The article states that both rebuilt houses 'im Jahr 2017 ... ins Denkmalverzeichnis eingetragen wurden' -- the RECONSTRUCTIONS were listed, in their own right, as evidence of West German reconstruction practice. That is a listing of a 1986-89 building and not of a 1529 one, and it is the reason this record's `dates.altered` is as long as it is.

survey.prepared: The German (or French) Wikipedia article, read as CONTINUOUS PROSE IN AN EXTRACT. IT IS AN ENCYCLOPEDIA ARTICLE AND NOT A SURVEY OR A REGISTER. Germany's monument registers are held per Land and the Land databases reachable from this container print a one-line Schutzbegruendung rather than a HABS-style description, so the fullest description available is this. Every figure taken from it carries the same warning on the measurement itself: a number sourced here is NOT of the same standing as one from a HABS data page or a Historic England Details section, and it should not be read as one merely because it sits in the same field of the same schema.

quotes.text: Das in der Konstruktion noch spätgotische Fachwerkgebäude mit seiner repräsentativen, 26 Meter hochaufragenden Schmuckfassade galt den Hildesheimern – unter Berufung auf eine Bemerkung von Eugène Viollet-le-Duc – als „das schönste Fachwerkhaus der Welt“.
quotes.page: German Wikipedia, 'Knochenhaueramtshaus (Hildesheim)', section on the first restoration. Not paginated. Footnote markers rendered by the extract as stray parentheses have been dropped and no word was changed.

quotes.text: In der ursprünglichen Nutzung wurden neben dem Verkaufsraum die Kellergewölbe als Lagerraum verwendet. Im ersten Stock wurden Sitzungen der Gilde abgehalten, und in den weiteren Obergeschossen waren Vorratsräume sowie Wohnungen untergebracht.
quotes.page: German Wikipedia, 'Knochenhaueramtshaus (Hildesheim)', section on the early building history. Not paginated.

measurements.name: facade_height_ft
measurements.note: 26 metres, converted at 3.28084 ft/m. THE ONLY HEIGHT THE WHOLE GERMANIC CLUSTER PRODUCED, and it is the height of a decorated facade rather than of a wall or a storey -- a jettied guild house whose front runs up through several storeys into the gable. It is a figure about the FRONT, and reading it as an eaves height would be wrong. SOURCE IS AN ENCYCLOPEDIA ARTICLE, not a survey; the building it describes is the 1986-89 reconstruction of the 1529 house.

note: Tranche 3, Germanic cluster, 5 September 2026. The node's own exemplar note already carries the caveat that this is a reconstruction, and the record sharpens it: the German monument register listed the REBUILT houses in 2017, and it listed them as evidence of West German reconstruction practice rather than as sixteenth-century fabric. Any figure taken from this building is a figure about a drawing that was executed in the 1980s.
